requirements.description: Fellowships are provided to excellent researchers undertaking international mobility, with applications made jointly by the researcher and a beneficiary in the academic or non-academic sector.
European Postdoctoral Fellowships are open to researchers of any nationality coming to Europe from any country or moving within Europe, with a standard duration between 12 and 24 months.

Global Postdoctoral Fellowships are open to European nationals or long-term residents, requiring an outgoing phase (12-24 months) in a non-associated Third Country and a mandatory 12-month return phase to an EU Member State or Associated Country host.

An optional secondment phase within the overall duration of the fellowship may be included in any country worldwide, as a single period or shorter mobility periods, subject to the applicable secondment limits.

An optional non-academic placement of up to six months at the end of the project may be requested, at a non-academic host in an EU Member State or Associated Country; the request must be an integral, evaluated part of the proposal.

Training activities must integrate transferable skills including digital skills (e.g. generative AI), foster Open Science, knowledge valorisation, and research integrity, and prepare fellows for research collaboration enabled by digital technologies (FAIR data, citizen science, etc.).
A Career Development Plan must be jointly established by the supervisor(s) and researcher and submitted as a deliverable at the beginning of the action.

Fellowships in Euratom-covered research areas are conditionally eligible only where organisations active in nuclear research are established in an EU Member State or Euratom-associated country, and are supported by the Euratom Programme.
ERA Fellowships (implemented through Work Programme Annex 11, Widening Participation) conditionally provide support for fellowships undertaken in a widening country.
